newsitem.title: USA: Chevron Calif. gasoline unit up this weekend.
newsitem.headline: Chevron Calif. gasoline unit up this weekend.

text.p: A 60,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) isomax unit at Chevron's Corp's Richmond, Calif., refinery will resume full production this weekend, after a crack cut output 25 percent this week, a plant source said.
The unit has lost about 15,000 bpd of gasoline output since the start of the week, said the source, who declined to be identified.
"It's up this weekend," the source said, adding the plant's total gasoline output was 200,000 bpd.
About 20 to 30 percent of the isomax's output is jet fuel, with the rest gasoline.
While small, the unit's loss of aviation fuel has kept wholesale jet prices firm this week on the West Coast amid problems at other refineries.
"The jet loss is a lot. All the hydrocrackers have been down," said one refined products broker, referring to the planned shutdowns at Mobil and Exxon's unit earlier this year.

"Tosco's is still down from the fire. All of them make a little jet, but all together, they make a lot of jet," he said, referring to a late January explosion at Tosco's Avon, Calif. hydrocracker, which has a 32,000 bpd capacity.
The unit is reportedly due up in June.
Jet fuel prices have stayed firm this week, rising three cents since March 25 to 64.50/65.50 cents a gallon Friday.
In the same period, wholesale unleaded gasoline prices in California fell 14 percent.
